claims.text: The stress-strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by interaction between thermal-expansion mismatch and mechanical loading.
The thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is governed by interaction between thermal-expansion mismatch and mechanical loading.
Thermal-expansion mismatch induces internal stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
Mismatch-induced internal stresses interact with mechanical loading.
The interaction of internal stress with mechanical loading affects alloy strength.
Grain boundaries are a structural mediator of the proposed behavior.
Dislocation networks are a structural mediator of the proposed behavior.
The investigated material is polycrystalline HfNbTaTiZr.
At 1000 K, the proposed treatment will increase yield strength by 15% relative to the baseline.
At 1000 K, the proposed treatment will decrease the thermal-expansion coefficient by 20% relative to the baseline.
The relevant test window is 293–1250 K and 0–500 MPa.
The exact internal stresses and their interaction with loading may depend on microstructure and loading conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if the yield-strength increase is below 5% or the thermal-expansion-coefficient decrease is below 10% at 1000 K.

contradictions.description: The baseline is an unloaded state at 293 K, whereas outcomes are evaluated under combined loading at 1000 K. Thus temperature and loading state both change, so the comparison does not isolate thermal-expansion mismatch as the governing cause.

The prediction specifies 15% strengthening and a 20% expansion-coefficient decrease, but falsification only occurs below 5% or 10%, respectively. Intermediate results are neither the stated prediction nor falsifying, leaving an unresolved outcome region.
